subject: general
question: Rahul invested a certain sum for two years at 60% p.a. compound interest, compounded annually. If at the end of two years he received interest of ₹11,700, then how much did he initially invest?
solution:
Given: 

Rate of interest = 60%

Time (n) = 2 years

Interest = ₹11,700

Concept used:

Compound interest, CI = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ - P

where

P = Principal amount

R = Rate of interest per year

N = Time in years

Calculation:

Let the initial investment (Principal amount) be P.

According to the question,

P(1 + 60/100)² - P= 11700

⇒ P × 1.6² - P = 11700

⇒ P × 2.56 - P = 11700

⇒ P (2.56 - 1) = 11700

⇒ P × 1.56 = 11700

⇒ P = 11700/1.56

⇒ P = 7500

**∴ He initially invested ₹7,500.**
